prior_year_events.impact_description: Increase in the cumulative gross claims incurred for the 2021 underwriting year (from 50,500 to 56,147 thousand USD), resulting in an adverse prior year development.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2023 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding closed at $123.965m (2023) versus $53.078m at 31 December 2022. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates adverse prior-year development driven by the 2021 underwriting year (an increase of approximately $5.647m), reflecting adverse claims development and inflationary/IBNR recalibration pressures, predominantly affecting casualty/thirdparty liability exposures.
raw_causal_phrases: Cyber The rapidly changing environment in the cyber class of business has a higher degree of uncertainty due to the propensity for changes to the cyber risk landscape and perils, such as ransomware emerging in the past couple of years.
Rate change Loss estimates are heavily influenced by expected loss ratios on which there is a high level of uncertainty.
Inflation Continued focus remained on inflation throughout 2023 due to the continuing war in Ukraine as well as other supply side issues.
data.data_quality_notes: All amounts are reported in the syndicate's native currency (USD). Opening reserves taken from the prior-year closing gross claims outstanding on the Statement of Financial Position (page 21). No explicit gross prior-year movement figure was provided; prior-year development was derived from the gross claims development triangle (pages 44-45) using the standard diagonal comparison method and includes only the 2021 underwriting year (2022 and 2023 excluded). exact_reserve_text is empty because no single sentence explicitly quantified the gross prior year movement. Confidence reflects use of the triangle as primary source for prior-year movement.
